transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-19 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (CTO), Alex (Infra), Nina (Sec Eng), Samir (ML Eng)

Auto-summary: Short kickoff covering environment access, security questions (KMS, audit logs), pilot timeline and perf goals. Action items captured.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um I think we have most folks here, we're going to run through the onboarding intake and try to lock down staging access and the pilot scope. Quick intros?
[00:12] Jordan (CTO): Jordan here - CTO at LumenForge, I'll be sponsoring the pilot.
[00:15] Alex (Infra): Alex - infra lead, I'll coordinate VPC peering and networking.
[00:18] Nina (Security): Nina, security eng, I'll own compliance checks.
[00:21] Samir (ML): Samir, ML engineer, will run the workload tests.
[00:24] Maya (AE): Great, Redwood side Daniel our SE will cover the technical checklist and Priya will own the onboarding plan.
[00:30] Daniel (SE): Hi all, quick note, excited to dig in. I put a draft runbook in the chat, it's the staging checklist, but I'll go over the high-level items now.

[00:45] [00:45] Daniel (SE): So first, access model. LumenForge wants to evaluate both Hosted and Dedicated modes; for pilot we recommend starting hosted for speed, but with a private VPC connection so you can validate network egress and logging. Correction: when I say hosted with VPC I mean Redwood Hosted w/ VPC Egress, not the full private deploy. There's sometimes mix-up with 'Redwood Privateer' in notes, but that's the on‑prem option.
[01:10] Nina (Security): Quick question, what about key management? We need BYOK and HSM options. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS?
[01:18] Daniel (SE): Yes, we support KMS integrations. For hosted pilot we can use customer KMS via cross-account key policies (we'll document). For Dedicated or Private installs, full HSM/KMS integration is supported. There can be a slight latency delta for KMS calls if you use external HSM, worth noting for tight latency SLOs.

[01:45] [01:45] Alex (Infra): Ok networking — we prefer not to do peering immediately. Is there a temporary pattern? A tunnel or jumpbox?
[01:52] Priya (CSM): We usually start with read-only staging access: Redwood SE gets a bastion IP for the staging subnet, then we move to a peered VPC for the benchmark week. We'll put the exact CIDR and ephemeral keys in the intake doc.

[02:10] Samir (ML): On the performance side — our baseline is 150 req/s with 512 tokens avg and p50 latency target 200ms. Can Redwood meet that with the medium model we selected?
[02:19] Daniel (SE): We'll run a quick sizing estimate, but initial thought: for 512 avg tokens and 150 rps you'll likely want Dedicated pool or reserve burst; hosted with autoscaling might also work but cost and tail latency differ. We'll propose two configs in the runbook. Also note, tokenization and prefix cache shape matter — if you have longer conversation history the KV cache hit rate changes.

[02:50] [02:50] Jordan (CTO): Also important: data residency. Our customers in EMEA require data to not leave eu-west-1. Can pilot be run in eu-west?
[02:58] Maya (AE): Yes, we have hosted regions in eu-west and can pin the pilot region. For Dedicated or Private you can choose on‑prem or local cloud. We'll include region pinning in the pilot constraints.

[03:20] Nina (Security): SOC2 and audit logs — can you provide the SOC2 report and show how audit logs can be exported to our SIEM?
[03:27] Priya (CSM): Absolutely — I'll drop the SOC2 artifact and the log-forwarding guide after the call. Our dashboards can stream to your Splunk or S3; we'll include a sample lambda to shuttle logs if you prefer.

[03:50] [03:50] Alex (Infra): About credentials lifecycle — we need short-lived credentials. Are there built-in token rotation APIs?
[03:57] Daniel (SE): Yes, short-lived tokens and role-based access via IAM mapping. For Private deployments we support your internal IAM/OIDC; for Hosted we offer scoped API keys with expiry and key rotation endpoints. Some of the docs call it 'Redwood Concole' which is typoed, but the console supports key revocation.

[04:20] Samir (ML): Could we run a small proof that uses our real sample prompts? We have PII redaction concerns — we'd like to know how data is retained.
[04:29] Maya (AE): Completely reasonable. Retention defaults are retention-disabled for inputs after 30 days, but for pilots we can enable no-retention and show your audit logs. We'll add data handling options to the intake doc.

[04:50] [04:50] Nina (Security): Encryption at rest? Are embeddings stored? We don't want customer data persisted unless explicitly allowed.
[04:58] Daniel (SE): Embeddings may be cached for perf; we can disable embedding caching for your pilot or scope it to ephemeral caches. All stored data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if requested. There's a config flag in the runtime for persistent cache.

[05:20] Jordan (CTO): Great. Timeline — we'd like pilot in two weeks. Realistic?
[05:27] Priya (CSM): Two weeks is tight but doable for a scoped benchmark: day 1 access + small smoke tests, day 3–5 perf run & collect, week 2 analysis and next-step decision. Daniel, do you agree?
[05:35] Daniel (SE): Yes, with staging access and sample traces from Samir, we can hit that. Biggest blockers are VPC access and KMS policy approvals.

[06:00] [06:00] Alex (Infra): Our security team insists on an external pen-test window before any peering. How do customers usually handle that?
[06:08] Maya (AE): Two approaches: a short external scan in staging, or we provision a dedicated isolated environment for their pen-test. For pilot we can do the scan in our staging infra with scoped IP whitelists. We'll share the pen-test playbook.

[06:30] Nina (Security): Ok please send pen-test checklist and expected schedule.

[06:40] Samir (ML): Quick question about model versions — we want to compare two open models and a quantized variant. Can Redwood host multiple model versions and route based on a canary policy?
[06:49] Daniel (SE): Yes, model versioning and rollouts are supported, we can do canary traffic splits and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants. For the bench we'll do per-model runs to compare latency + quality. Note sometimes the product doc has 'model catalog with redwood-verified performance proflies' — typos in auto notes but the feature exists.

[07:15] [07:15] Jordan (CTO): What about cost visibility? We need token-level cost breakdown during the pilot so finance can see expected run rate.
[07:23] Priya (CSM): Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. We'll enable a two-week cost dashboard for you and share sample CSV export.

[07:50] Alex (Infra): On the networking side can you share the exact egress IPs? We need them for firewall rules.
[07:57] Daniel (SE): We'll provide an ephemeral list for staging and then stable NAT IPs for Dedicated. I'll include that in the runbook.

[08:20] [08:20] Maya (AE): Let's collect success criteria. Jordan?
[08:25] Jordan (CTO): Primary: p50 < 200ms at 150 rps for common prompt profile. Secondary: no PII leakage and SOC2 audit checklist completed. Budget wise we want to see an estimate below $Xk monthly for steady state.
[08:40] Maya (AE): Noted — we'll return cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated.

[09:00] [09:00] Samir (ML): For the perf benchmark I'll push a sample workload generator and a set of 10 representative prompts. Does Redwood have a preferred load driver or should we use wrk-type?
[09:08] Daniel (SE): We'll share a reference harness (python + async clients). Wrk-style drivers are ok but our harness includes token accounting and KV cache shaping to mimic production traffic. We'll share it and can execute runs on your behalf if you prefer.

[09:40] Alex (Infra): Any compliance docs re: EU data transfer? We need DPA appendices.
[09:46] Priya (CSM): We'll share the DPA and standard data processing addendum. If you need a specific clause for data residency we'll escalate legal.

[10:10] [10:10] Jordan (CTO): Is there support for canary A/B tests? We want to route 10% to a new model variant during rollout.
[10:16] Daniel (SE): Yes — rollout policies support traffic splitting, automatic fallback on latency or error thresholds. We'll include an example policy.

[10:40] Maya (AE): Anything else blocking for the two-week pilot start?
[10:45] Nina (Security): Need SOC2 artifact, pen-test checklist, KMS integration docs.
[10:50] Jordan (CTO): We need the runbook and a cost estimate.
[10:54] Alex (Infra): Staging CIDR and whitelisted bastion IP for SE.

[11:10] [11:10] Priya (CSM): Ok recap: Redwood will send runbook, SOC2, pen-test checklist, demo harness and the VPC/access checklist by end of week; customer to provide staging CIDR, sample prompts, and sample traces.
[11:26] Samir (ML): I'll upload prompts and traces to the S3 link Priya shares.

[11:40] [11:40] Maya (AE): Great, we'll schedule the benchmark slot for Apr 27th window. I'll send invites after this call.

[11:55] Jordan (CTO): Cool, looking forward to it.
[12:00] Maya (AE): Thanks everyone, we wrapped a bit early, but that's good.

Post-call notes:
- Some transcription artifacts: product names misheard (Redwood Console -> Concole, Private -> Privateer) in auto notes; clarified in call.
- Tone: collaborative, security-savvy buyer asking for KMS/HSM and pen-test.

Shared links mentioned: runbook draft (link placeholder), SOC2 artifact (link placeholder), pen-test playbook (link placeholder), benchmark harness (link placeholder).

End of transcript.
